what: A strict upper bound for the number of integer remainder-coefficient arrays: for B>0,c≥1 and c n D≤N/2 with N>0, (2 floor(B^c)+1)^(nD)<(B+1)^N.
how: Uses floor_rpow_count_lt_aux to bound one coefficient count by (B+1)^(2c), then pow_lt_pow_left₀, Real.rpow_mul_natCast and exponent monotonicity; handles nD=0 using one_lt_pow₀.
hypotheses: B>0 gives positive real-power base and B+1>1.
c≥1 supplies power superadditivity in the floor-count helper.
N>0 retains strictness in the zero-dimensional case.
c n D≤N/2 is the weak exponent budget; n,D may be zero.

generalization.verified:
theorem powerBudget {a b t : ℝ} {k N : ℕ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 1 < b)
    (hbase : a < b ^ t) (hN : 0 < N) (hbudget : t * k ≤ N) : a ^ k < b ^ N
generalization.semantic: Arbitrary a,b,t separate count generation from exponent lifting; permits other coefficient-count bounds. Flattening nD to k alone is only representation normalization.
generalization.hypothesis_localization: N positivity can be localized to k=0 in verified localizedBudget; exact target cannot drop it because nD=0 is allowed.
generalization.sharpness: B0,c0,N0/no-budget and positive c=1/2 counterexamples compile. No claim that c>=1 is sharp or that current hypotheses are globally maximal.
